Plan, organize, lead and supervise formal and structured specialized arts programs for child/youth and adults including drawing, painting, drama and music programs


**Responsibilities:**


* Develop progressive lesson plan specific to the abilities of each group
* Demonstrate, instruct and lead participants through a set of specific skills
* Supervise and evaluate participants progress throughout the program
* Monitor and keep inventory of program supplies, inform Program Coordinator when supplies need replenishing

* Perform safety check of equipment prior to being used
* Keep accurate participant attendance records
* Follow up with full\-time staff regarding participants with extended absences
* Directly guide volunteers as required

**Requirements:**


* Currently enrolled in or completed a post\-secondary arts program is considered an asset
* Five (5\) years experience participating in the related discipline
* Two (2\) years experience instructing in the related discipline
* Possess and keep current Intermediate/Standard First Aid/CPR ‘C’ qualifications
* Demonstrate good customer service and communication skills to deal effectively and courteously with staff and the general public; good interpersonal skills with the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships
* Attend all staff trainings and meetings
* Ability to work shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required

This may include data organization and processing of large functional and structural MRI data, quality control for ongoing studies, and timely implementation of neuroimaging pipelines for decisions in clinical trials. You will also be required to assist in data entry; updating and maintaining electronic databases; conducting searches of electronic resources; as well as preparing data for presentations and peer\-reviewed research papers. Other research related administrative duties are also required. Current projects focus on using imaging markers to identify disease trajectories under various treatment regimes, including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and pharmacotherapies. Job Description: The Kimel Family Translational Imaging\-Genetics Laboratory is a large multidisciplinary research laboratory dedicated to discovering the causes of severe mental illness and advancing treatments for severe mental illness. The focus of the laboratory is using brain imaging to understand human brain function, psychiatric illness, and treatment outcomes. The laboratory is located in the Brain Health Imaging Centre. The lab includes a group of PIs; Drs. Nicholas Neufeld, Peter Zhukovsky, Colin Hawco, Erin Dickie, Lindsay Oliver, Aristotle Voineskos, and Stephanie Ameis, as well as other collaborating scientists.


We are seeking a full\-time, contract (12 months) Research Analyst who will provide support to the Kimel Family Lab’s research team and projects. The Research Analyst will be part of a dynamic multi\-disciplinary team of psychiatrists, neuroscientists, engineers, and clinical researchers interested in understanding brain function and dysfunction.


The Research Analyst will provide support in maintaining neuroimaging data collected from multiple research studies and will assist in quality control and analysis of this data. This may include data organization and processing of large functional and structural MRI data, quality control for ongoing studies, and timely implementation of neuroimaging pipelines for decisions in clinical trials. You will also be required to assist in data entry; updating and maintaining electronic databases; conducting searches of electronic resources; as well as preparing data for presentations and peer\-reviewed research papers. Other research related administrative duties are also required. Current projects focus on using imaging markers to identify disease trajectories under various treatment regimes, including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and pharmacotherapies. You will support a healthy workplace that embraces diversity, encourages teamwork and complies with all applicable CAMH policies, as well as all regulatory and legislative requirements.


This position is located at 250 College Street and travel between sites may be required.


  
Responsibilities
  
Qualifications

The successful candidate must possess an Honours Bachelor’s Degree in computer science, psychology, neuroscience, or a related discipline combined 1\-year relevant research experience and proficiency with programming languages (e.g., Python, R). Experience in MRI analysis tools (i.e. Freesurfer, FSL, SPM, BIDS, nilearn) and/or neuroscience is an asset. Experience with Linux computing in a high\-performance computing environment as well as system administration tasks (e.g., networking, database management) is an asset. The lab includes a group of PIs; Drs. Nicholas Neufeld, Peter Zhukovsky, Colin Hawco, Erin Dickie, Lindsay Oliver, Aristotle Voineskos, and Stephanie Ameis, as well as other collaborating scientists.


We are seeking a full\-time, contract (12 months) Research Analyst who will provide support to the Kimel Family Lab’s research team and projects. The Research Analyst will be part of a dynamic multi\-disciplinary team of psychiatrists, neuroscientists, engineers, and clinical researchers interested in understanding brain function and dysfunction.


The Research Analyst will provide support in maintaining neuroimaging data collected from multiple research studies and will assist in quality control and analysis of this data. This may include data organization and processing of large functional and structural MRI data, quality control for ongoing studies, and timely implementation of neuroimaging pipelines for decisions in clinical trials. You will also be required to assist in data entry; updating and maintaining electronic databases; conducting searches of electronic resources; as well as preparing data for presentations and peer\-reviewed research papers. Other research related administrative duties are also required. Current projects focus on using imaging markers to identify disease trajectories under various treatment regimes, including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and pharmacotherapies. You will support a healthy workplace that embraces diversity, encourages teamwork and complies with all applicable CAMH policies, as well as all regulatory and legislative requirements.


This position is located at 250 College Street and travel between sites may be required.

Qualifications

The successful candidate must possess an Honours Bachelor’s Degree in computer science, psychology, neuroscience, or a related discipline combined 1\-year relevant research experience and proficiency with programming languages (e.g., Python, R). Experience in MRI analysis tools (i.e. Freesurfer, FSL, SPM, BIDS, nilearn) and/or neuroscience is an asset. Experience with Linux computing in a high\-performance computing environment as well as system administration tasks (e.g., networking, database management) is an asset. Experience with statistical packages (R, SPSS, SAS, and MATLAB) and data interpretation is an asset. Excellent interpersonal, communication (oral/written) and organizational skills are required, along with the ability to collaborate effectively with team members. The successful candidate will be detail\-oriented and be able to exercise initiative, and good judgment and will have the ability to multi\-task and produce high\-quality, accurate work while meeting program deadlines and requirements. The successful candidate requires the ability to work effectively in a variety of settings with individuals from diverse backgrounds.

(Fall Semester: September 9th, 2026 – December 8th, 2026, Fridays 11:50-2:50pm; In-Person)
COURSE DESCRIPTION:
This course grounds theory and methods of research practices within a framework of Indigenous knowledge and decolonizing principles - specifically OCAD University's Indigenous Learning Outcomes. Diverse cultural perspectives are prioritized through workshops and seminars introducing research ethics to learn about the positive and negative impacts research can have on participants and their environment. Exploring, searching, discovering, and analyzing research data support ways to express findings in novel ways. Differences between ethical and unethical techniques of community research are examined through intersectional contexts demonstrating plural outcomes, enabling researchers to formulate critical questions to make informed decisions.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching and teaching-related responsibilities may include but are not limited
to:
course outline development, studio preparation and delivery inclusive of lectures, critiques, grading, mid-term evaluations and final evaluations/reviews; guiding students through iterative, research-based design processes from user analysis through prototyping; providing timely and constructive feedback on studio work; and maintaining an accessible and inclusive studio environment. Responsibilities may also include drafting or modifying a course-based Research Ethics Board (REB) application as needed to support student research activities. Responsibility for health & safety and meeting academic and curricular requirements and deadlines is also expected.
QUALIFICATIONS:
The successful applicant should have a Bachelor’s degree in advertising,
graphic design or relevant discipline and/or equivalent professional/practical experience. Outstanding communication skills, and a demonstrated capacity to support and resource independent studio investigations are essential to teaching at this level. A demonstrated commitment to the principles of equity and diversity, and proven ability to work effectively and collegially with a diverse population of students & faculty underpin all academic positions at
OCADU.
A current body of work within Advertising or the professional creative field (as it relates to advertising) and/or academic disciplines as it relates to the course description(s).
Experience with, and aptitude for, highly iterative, process-oriented work without the restriction of fixed outcomes or expectations.
An asset: two (2) years of teaching experience at the undergraduate level in a related Design discipline.
Demonstrated leadership and experience in promoting a respectful and inclusive work and learning environment for students, staff, and Faculty.
TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:
Sessional appointments are fixed-term annual contracts. Sessional compensation includes a per-course pay scale with salary level of
$7,508.00 (per 0.5 credit course)
plus 7% in lieu of benefits and vacation pay, per the provisions of the Employment Standards Act. These positions are subject to budgetary approval and satisfactory enrolment levels.

A statement of teaching philosophy that responds to the profile of the position;

link or web address
to your digital portfolio of recent and current work/publications (if applicable)

Plan, organize, lead and supervise formal and structured specialized arts programs for child/youth and adults including drawing, painting, drama and music programs


**Responsibilities:**


* Develop progressive lesson plan specific to the abilities of each group
* Demonstrate, instruct and lead participants through a set of specific skills
* Supervise and evaluate participants progress throughout the program
* Monitor and keep inventory of program supplies, inform Program Coordinator when supplies need replenishing
* Administer first aid as required and complete Public Accident/Incident Reports or Complaint/Enquiry Forms as required

* Keep accurate participant attendance records
* Follow up with full\-time staff regarding participants with extended absences
* Directly guide volunteers as required

**Requirements:**


* Currently enrolled in or completed a post\-secondary arts program is considered an asset
* Five (5\) years experience participating in the related discipline
* Two (2\) years experience instructing in the related discipline
* Possess and keep current Intermediate/Standard First Aid/CPR ‘C’ qualifications
* Demonstrate good customer service and communication skills to deal effectively and courteously with staff and the general public; good interpersonal skills with the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships
* Attend all staff trainings and meetings
* Ability to work shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required

Job Description: The Kimel Family Translational Imaging\-Genetics Laboratory is a large multidisciplinary research laboratory dedicated to discovering the causes of severe mental illness and advancing treatments for severe mental illness. The focus of the laboratory is using brain imaging to understand human brain function, psychiatric illness, and treatment outcomes. The laboratory is located in the Brain Health Imaging Centre. The lab includes a group of PIs; Drs. Nicholas Neufeld, Peter Zhukovsky, Colin Hawco, Erin Dickie, Lindsay Oliver, Aristotle Voineskos, and Stephanie Ameis, as well as other collaborating scientists.


We are seeking a full\-time, contract (12 months) Research Analyst who will provide support to the Kimel Family Lab’s research team and projects. The Research Analyst will be part of a dynamic multi\-disciplinary team of psychiatrists, neuroscientists, engineers, and clinical researchers interested in understanding brain function and dysfunction.


The Research Analyst will provide support in maintaining neuroimaging data collected from multiple research studies and will assist in quality control and analysis of this data. This may include data organization and processing of large functional and structural MRI data, quality control for ongoing studies, and timely implementation of neuroimaging pipelines for decisions in clinical trials. You will also be required to assist in data entry; updating and maintaining electronic databases; conducting searches of electronic resources; as well as preparing data for presentations and peer\-reviewed research papers. Other research related administrative duties are also required. Current projects focus on using imaging markers to identify disease trajectories under various treatment regimes, including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and pharmacotherapies. You will support a healthy workplace that embraces diversity, encourages teamwork and complies with all applicable CAMH policies, as well as all regulatory and legislative requirements.


This position is located at 250 College Street and travel between sites may be required.


  
Responsibilities
  
Qualifications
